clue.text: Investor in stock exchange loss

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters of the phrase stock exchange loss

explanation.surface: A City investor suffers a loss on the stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles two words: the end of 'exchange' and the start of 'loss'.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer who puts money into a theatrical show or a new business venture is called by this heavenly name.

clue.text: One who helps satanists in corruption

indicators.note: corruption suggests something spoiled or distorted, so the word satanists is jumbled

explanation.surface: A helper who corrupts devil-worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide or helper who supports someone in their work.

clue.text: A ball at the theatre?

explanation.definitionFit: A globe is a sphere, and the Globe was the London playhouse where Shakespeare's plays were staged.

clue.text: State team receiving money for big win

parts.note: land means a state or country

indicators.note: receiving means the team word takes in the money letter

parts.note: a side is a team
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A national team on a big bonus for a great victory.
explanation.definitionFit: An overwhelming election victory is said to be a sweeping triumph of this kind.

clue.text: Carefully chosen cheer-leader — her cheer is stirring

indicators.note: stirring means being mixed up, so the letters before it get jumbled
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of cheer in cheer-leader

explanation.surface: A cheerleader's chant is rousing the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer-leader' gives C, the first letter of 'cheer'; with HER CHEER that makes the letters that 'is stirring' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing describes something rare, exquisite and selected with great care.

clue.text: A different impression forming about the outcome

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an issue is a result or outcome

explanation.surface: A new impression forming about how things turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impression' here is a printing term: a fresh print run of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A new printing or edition of a book is a second impression of it.

clue.text: Card-carrying occupation?

parts.note: a profession or vocation whose name is carried on a visiting card, the kind left when paying a social visit

explanation.definitionFit: A vocation or profession, and a visiting card is known by the same name.

clue.text: Record run in unaccompanied ascent

indicators.note: in means the run letter goes inside
ascent means the word climbs, read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: lone means alone or unaccompanied
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A climber sets a record by going up solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascent' reverses ENOL upward in a down answer; R sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to register or record a name on a list.

clue.text: Taxi originally rented instead of hired carriage

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: originally means the first letters of rented, instead and of

parts.note: let means rented out or hired

explanation.surface: A taxi was rented first in place of a hired horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' picks first letters from three words: R, I, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, later the name of a convertible car.

clue.text: Cover-up on electors' first choice

indicators.note: on means placed on top of the next piece in a down entry
up means the word is read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a tile is a covering for a roof

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of electors'

explanation.surface: A scandal hushed up about voters' preferred candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' looks like a scandal but is TILE read upwards; the E from 'electors' first' goes under it.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the choice or pick of a group, the best.

clue.text: Club programme for a flyer

parts.note: a spoon is an old golf club, a lofted wooden one
a bill is a theatre programme or poster listing the acts

explanation.surface: A golf club's printed programme of events for a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird with a flat broad-tipped beak is a flying creature.

clue.text: A poor performer, not quite a teacher

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: in British sporting slang a rabbit is a weak player, especially a feeble batsman at cricket

explanation.surface: A dud entertainer who almost qualifies as a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT is British slang for a hopeless player, especially in cricket or tennis; 'not quite' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader is literally a master or teacher of the law.

clue.text: A Building Society loses

parts.note: a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: A building society suffers a financial loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building Society' looks like the British savings institution, but 'A building' is SHED and 'Society' is S.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off or drop something, like leaves or skin, is to lose it.

clue.text: Submit extremely bad animation for picture

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters, of Submit

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
life means animation, liveliness or vigour

explanation.surface: Turn in a really poor piece of cartoon work in place of a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a painting genre showing arranged inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers.

clue.text: A writer's attributable

definitions.note: the clue word is an adjective while the answer is a verb meaning to credit; the setter's 's (is) leans the reading towards a verb phrase

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A certain author's work can be credited to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'A writer's' reads as 'A scribe is', and the answer is the verb 'credit to', not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute or credit something to a source is the verb this adjective comes from in sense.

clue.text: Established understudy for an artist

parts.note: read as under-study: con means to study, and under says the next word sits beneath it in this down entry
stable means firmly established

explanation.surface: A settled stand-in for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understudy' looks like a stand-in actor; split it as 'under study'. John Constable was an English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English painter famous for landscapes such as The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Sea change that is legal

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sea change that happens to be lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea change' looks like a phrase, but 'Sea' is the definition and 'change' the anagram signal acting on IE and LEGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the freshwater lake in northern Israel known in the Bible as a sea, where Jesus walked on the water.

clue.text: Use field craft to enclose cattle when there is likelihood of escape

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
kine is an old plural of cow, meaning cattle
SS is a steamship, a seagoing craft

explanation.surface: Use rural skills to pen livestock when they might get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field craft' looks like countryside skill; it is LEA plus SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakiness is the state of letting liquid or gas escape.

clue.text: Task many performed

parts.note: an exercise is a task set for practice
D is 500 in Roman numerals, standing for many

explanation.surface: A job carried out by lots of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is the Roman numeral D, 500, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to perform or carry it out.

clue.text: Line of dynasty entangled but not bent

parts.note: Tang was a Chinese imperial dynasty

indicators.note: but not tells us to take the word entangled without a part of it

parts.note: angled means bent or crooked

explanation.surface: A family line from an ancient dynasty, intertwined yet never crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled but not bent' is ENT-ANGLED with ANGLED (bent) removed, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: Cup-holders seen here having drinks before the dance

parts.note: teas are drinks
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Trophy winners spotted here having refreshments before a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup-holders' suggests trophy winners, but means saucers or customers holding teacups at a cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe serving tea is where you see people holding cups.

clue.text: He receives money, perhaps, to give directions

parts.note: to grant is to give or bestow
E and E are two compass directions, east twice

explanation.surface: Someone paid money, maybe, to hand out instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' supplies two compass points, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A person awarded a grant or a legal transfer of property is its recipient.

clue.text: Payment for changing round, for example

indicators.note: changing means the letters are altered in order

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Payment received for giving change, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerdon is an archaic word for a reward or recompense.

clue.text: Assistance from starter holding or backing horse

indicators.note: holding means one word wraps round the others

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests the official at a race, but it is a first course; 'backing' turns only 'or', and the horse follows it inside.

clue.text: Expression of impatience from author after parking

indicators.note: after means the author comes after the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright and author

explanation.surface: An exasperated sigh from a writer who has just parked.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation of contempt or irritation, like 'bah'.

clue.text: Out and about, beyond the normal limits

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Out and about, going further than usual bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means eccentric or unconventional, past what is usual.

clue.text: The patriarch is a preacher at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of the word preacher

explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes the middle two letters of 'preacher', A and C.

clue.text: Only the Ancient Mariner was on a wide, wide sea

definitions.text: the Ancient Mariner was on a wide, wide sea

clue.text: Beethoven's fifth takes a little practice

parts.note: a bit means a little

explanation.surface: Beethoven's Fifth Symphony needs a bit of rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's fifth' looks like the symphony, but it means the fifth letter of his name.

clue.text: Boundaries reduce the risk of disputes

parts.note: to hedge is to protect against loss, as in hedging a bet
rows are quarrels or disputes

clue.text: At which point we unrope horse to run wild

clue.text: Pay out a note from allowance

parts.note: a stipend is a fixed regular allowance or salary
